catalog_quote: [p.83] 加茂话有 5 个声调：高平调 55、高降调 51、中降调 31、中平调 33 和低平调 11，变调不产生新调值。总体来说，加茂话的变调模式有词法变调、句义变调和句法变调三种。 … [p.84] 但它们仍未完全虚化成表形态的词头，所以依靠音高的变化体现这一语义功能。若语义进一步虚化，则其可能伴随着语音的轻声化，进而语法化为类别标记。加茂话常用的词头 kɯ³¹、mɯ³¹都可构成类属广泛的附加式合成词，此时两者要变读为轻声①。kɯ³¹来源于数字“一”，是加茂话中最能产的词头，指称范畴较为宽泛，可构成不同语义类别的词类，例如：kɯ⁰det⁵⁵“蹦”、kɯ⁰laːu⁵⁵“圆”、kɯ⁰tek⁵⁵“壁虎”、kɯ⁰ziau¹¹“明天”、kɯ⁰tsa⁵¹“菠萝”、kɯ⁰siak⁵⁵“垃圾”等。mɯ³¹本义不明，主要构成果菜类及粮食类名词，例如：mɯ⁰thum⁵⁵“石榴”、mɯ⁰luəŋ⁵⁵“槟榔”、mɯ⁰ŋou⁵⁵“糯稻”等。随着语义的彻底虚化，这两个词头已经变成了一种语法标记。 [fn.①] 文中轻声标 0 调。 … [p.84 sec.二] 加茂话的一些词在语流当中，不管前后相邻音节的语音条件如何，都以自身本调为条件发生变调，一律由高平调 55 调变成中平调 33 调，变调规则较为固定。人称代词 kau⁵⁵“我”、məi⁵⁵“你”、au⁵⁵“我们”、tei⁵⁵“咱们”、sau⁵⁵“你们”，副词 na⁵⁵“才”，连词 bɛ⁵⁵“和”，介词 haŋ⁵⁵“在”，方位词 lau⁵⁵“上”、taːu⁵⁵“下”、su⁵⁵“里”，系词 tsaŋ⁵⁵“是”，趋向动词 hai⁵⁵“去”及否定词 ŋɔ⁵⁵“不”等等，这些词在语流中一般都降低音高，变读为 33 调。 … [p.86] 而变调后的声调变轻，口气较为缓和，表达了说话者婉转温和的叙述口气。

new_statements.translation: [p.83] Jiamao has five tones: high level 55, high falling 51, mid falling 31, mid level 33 and low level 11; tone sandhi produces no new tone values. … [p.84] If the meaning is further bleached, this may be accompanied by phonetic neutral-tone weakening (轻声化), and further grammaticalization into a class marker. The common Jiamao prefixes kɯ- and mɯ- both form affixal compounds of broad class membership, and in that case both must be read in the neutral (light, unstressed) tone. kɯ- derives from the numeral 'one' and is the most productive prefix in Jiamao … e.g. kɯ⁰det 'jump', kɯ⁰lau 'round', kɯ⁰tek 'gecko', kɯ⁰ziau 'tomorrow' … [fn.1] In this paper the neutral tone is written as tone 0. … [p.84] The personal pronouns kau 'I', məi 'you' …, the conjunction bɛ 'and', the preposition haŋ 'at' …, the copula tsaŋ, the directional verb hai 'go' and the negator ŋɔ 'not', etc., generally lower their pitch in connected speech and are read with tone 33.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Jiamao is a tone language (5 tones on every full syllable); the source states no lexical word-stress rule. Its only prominence statements: grammaticalized prefixes kɯ-, mɯ- are atonic/unstressed (轻声, 'tone 0') before a full-toned root, i.e. prefixed words are weak-strong (iambic, root-final prominence); high-level-tone function words (pronouns, negator, copula, adpositions, 'go') are prosodically weakened (55 -> 33, 'lighter') in running speech unless emphasized.
new_statements.exceptions: Citation (unsandhied) tone is retained on function words for emphasis/sentence-initial conditional ŋɔ and clause-final bɛ; class-term first members of 'class+specific' compounds lower 55->33 but are explicitly said NOT (yet) to be neutral-toned.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern prefix+root words and function words in connected speech (speaker 黄仁清, b.1963, 金不弄村, 加茂镇, Baoting county); no statement about stress placement in plain disyllabic compounds or citation forms beyond tone.
new_statements.identity_note: All first-hand data are the Jiamao 加茂镇 variety of Baoting county (Wu 2020: 加答村委会金不弄村; Ouyang & Zheng/Norquest: 加茂 point) = Glottolog jiam1236 [jio]. Chinese sources call it 黎语加茂方言/赛方言; the Lingshui variety is called 台 Tai. Norquest 2007/2015 and Thurgood 1992 treat Jiamao as a non-Hlai language (possible isolate with Hlai loan strata), so family-level Tai-Kadai/Hlai generalizations (e.g. van der Hulst 2010 'all tonal, monosyllabic') should not be transferred to it without a Jiamao-specific source.

sources.note: Tone language with 5 tones (55, 51, 31, 33, 11); sandhi creates no new values. No 重音 (stress) rule stated. p.84: the productive prefixes kɯ- (<'one') and mɯ- are pronounced as 轻声 (neutral/light tone, written tone 0) before the full-toned root; pp.84-86: pronouns, adverbs, the conjunction, preposition, localizers, copula, 'go' and the negator lower 55->33 in running speech ('降低音高'); citation tone = emphatic, sandhi tone described as '变轻' (lighter).

sources.note: Historical-comparative. Gives Jiamao register/tone values (p.335: A 55/11, X 51/31, DL 53/31, DS 55/22, after Ouyang & Zheng 1983) and initial/rime correspondences; argues Jiamao is a non-Hlai isolate with Hlai loan strata. Stress is mentioned only for reconstructed Pre-Hlai (iambic sesquisyllables, pp.250-251; stress-to-weight hypothesis rejected p.288). No synchronic statement on Jiamao word stress.
